fact: Deer Meadows Metropolitan District governs Mariana Butte 14th Subdivision, known as The Masters, a golf course community of custom homes, and its Architectural Control Committee reviews applications before they go to the City of Loveland.
quote: The following is intended as an outline of design and Architectural Development Standards (A.D.S.) that will apply to the construction of the Mariana Butte 14th Subdivision a.k.a. “The Masters”. An Architectural Control Committee (ACC) has been formed by the Deer Meadows Metropolitan District (the governing body) to review all applications for compliance with these criteria prior to submittal to the City of Loveland for review. … The Masters shall create a unique golf course community of custom home types linked by the existing golf course, open space, pedestrian walks, and natural areas with mature trees intended to maintain the riparian habitat, and incredible vistas.
source_label: Deer Meadows Metropolitan District, The Masters at Mariana Butte Architectural and Design Guidelines (Design Criteria updated 6/27/2023), introduction and Community Concept and Character
notes: PDF (16 pages) downloaded and read 2026-09-26 from the district's Architectural Control page. The district's site names itself 'Deer Meadows Metropolitan District'; the guidelines' first line says 'Deer Meadow Metropolitan District'.

fact: The Masters' design guidelines permit artificial turf with the Architectural Control Committee's approval, list it with xeriscape and hardscape under Lawn, require approval for turf on a front porch or balcony, and keep living grass at least four feet from a home's foundation.
quote: Lawn: Xeriscape, hardscape and non-vegetative turf grass (artificial turf) are permitted upon approval by the ACC. All vegetative turf areas shall be seeded or sod and shall be kept at least four (4) feet away from the foundation of the home or as recommended by a professional soil engineer or landscape professional, to ensure proper drainage is maintained. … ARTIFICIAL TURF — Non-vegetative turf is permitted upon approval by the ACC. Artificial grass products or other floor coverings to be used on a front porch or balcony must be approved by the ACC prior to installation.
source_label: Deer Meadows Metropolitan District, The Masters at Mariana Butte Architectural and Design Guidelines (Design Criteria updated 6/27/2023), Lawn and Specific Types of Improvements: Artificial Turf
notes: The source prints 'prior to installation..' (double period). Neither the guidelines nor the covenants mention putting greens.

fact: The Masters' design guidelines were first adopted on November 4, 2019, and their Fencing, Lawn, Artificial Turf and Solar Devices sections were revised on March 6, 2023.
quote: THESE DESIGN GUIDELINES WERE INTIALLY ADOPTED BY THE BOARD, on the 4th day of November, 2019. Document Revisions: Compliance to State and Local law, page 1. The Fencing Section, Lawn, Artificial Turf, Solar Devices (pages 4, 8, 10, 11, 12, 15, 16) of this document was revised on March 6, 2023
source_label: Deer Meadows Metropolitan District, The Masters at Mariana Butte Architectural and Design Guidelines (Design Criteria updated 6/27/2023), adoption and revision note
notes: 'INTIALLY' is the source's spelling. The page footers read 'Updated: 6/27/2023'.

fact: The Masters' 2008 covenants require grass, shrubs and trees to be kept in a healthy, live and growing condition, and allow landscaping changes only after board approval and never in a way that alters the approved drainage plan without it.
quote: e. All grass, shrubs and trees shall be kept and maintained in an attractive, healthy, live and growing condition, and all dead or diseased grass areas, shrubs and trees shall be promptly removed and replaced with suitable replacement landscaping. Each Lot shall be maintained with the landscaping as approved by the Board in good condition. f. Any changes to landscaping may be done only after approval of the Board in accordance with the procedures set forth in Article II hereof and under no circumstances may landscaping be changed or altered so as to affect the natural historic flow of water or the approved Drainage Plan without the prior approval of the Board.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, Easements and Restrictions for the Deer Meadows Metropolitan District property (made March 1, 2008; Larimer County reception 20080057629), Sec. 5.8(e) and (f)
notes: 18-page scanned PDF with a text layer, read 2026-09-26 from the district's Governing Documents page. The district's Rules and Regulations (Appendix A, E.3) repeat the 'attractive, healthy, live and growing condition' wording.

fact: The Masters' guidelines require ACC approval before a lot's first landscaping and any later material change to it, suggest submitting plans at least 45 days before work, and treat plans the ACC has not acted on within 45 days of acknowledging receipt as approved.
quote: In accordance with the recorded CC & R's, all improvements to a residential lot must be approved by the ACC prior to beginning construction on the Improvement. This requirement applies to permanent structures only, such as fences, decks, house and garage additions, storage sheds over twenty-five square feet, play structures and equipment, retaining walls and spas. This requirement also applies to the initial landscaping on a residential lot, as well as subsequent material changes to landscaping. It is suggested that plans for an Improvement be submitted at least 45 days prior to the commencement of the work on the Improvement, to allow time for the ACC to review the plans. In the event submitted plans and specifications are not acted upon by the ACC (i.e. written approval, disapproval or request for additional information or materials) within forty-five (45) days of acknowledgement of receipt, the plan shall be considered approved.
source_label: Deer Meadows Metropolitan District, The Masters at Mariana Butte Architectural and Design Guidelines (Design Criteria updated 6/27/2023), Procedures for Submission of Plans
notes: The same guidelines (Painting, item 8) refer to a 'THIRTY (30) DAY REVIEW TIME FRAME ALLOWED UNDER THE DECLARATION', and the recorded covenants (Sec. 2.2(d)) give the board 60 days and presume disapproval; the district's web page promises a response within 30 days. The documents do not agree.

fact: Deer Meadows Metropolitan District's Architectural Control Committee charges a $50 review fee, says it will respond within 30 days of a complete submission, and requires approved work to be finished within 1 year.
quote: Improvements or alterations on Lots within Deer Meadows Metro District are subject to review by the Architectural Control Committee (ACC). … There is a $50 Review Fee, which can be paid online through the portal or by check. The ACC will respond to your application within 30 days following complete submission. Approved improvements or alternations must be completed within 1 year following ACC approval.
source_label: Deer Meadows Metropolitan District, Architectural Control page
notes: Page read 2026-09-26 (HTTP 200). 'alternations' is the page's spelling.

fact: The Masters' recorded covenants require professionally prepared plans showing landscaping, grading, easements and utilities before any exterior change, and presume plans disapproved when the board neither approves nor disapproves them within 60 days.
quote: nor shall any exterior addition to or change or alteration of any Residence or improvement be made until professionally prepared plans and specifications with respect thereto (in manner and form designated within the Design Guidelines or otherwise satisfactory to the Board showing the proposed improvements, plot layout and all exterior elevations, materials and colors, landscaping, grading, easements and utilities, and such other information as may be reasonably requested by the Board) have been submitted to and been approved in writing by the Board. … If the Board fails either to approve or to disapprove such plans and specifications (including resubmission of disapproved plans and specifications which have been revised) within sixty (60) days after the same have been submitted to it (provided that all required information has been submitted), it shall be conclusively presumed that said plans and specifications have been disapproved
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, Easements and Restrictions for the Deer Meadows Metropolitan District property (made March 1, 2008), Sec. 2.2(a) and (d)
notes: Sec. 2.2 lets the board act itself or through an architectural control committee it forms.

fact: Deer Meadows' ACC application has separate boxes for front and rear landscaping, charges a $50.00 review fee on initial landscape submittals, and has the owner agree that ACC approval does not cover drainage or building permits, to call Colorado 811 for locates, and to make no change from the approved plan without written consent.
quote: B. My request involves the following type of improvement: ☐ Front Landscaping … ☐ Rear Landscaping … ACC approval does not constitute approval of the local building or zoning department, drainage design, structural or engineering safety and/or soundness. … I understand that it is my responsibility and obligation to obtain all required building permits, to contact Colorado 811 for utility locates, and to construct the Improvement in a workmanlike manner in conformance with all applicable easements, regulations, and building and zoning codes. … I understand that there shall be no deviations from the plans, specifications, and location approved by the ACC without prior written consent of the ACC. … Initial Landscape Submittals require a $50.00 Review Fee
source_label: Deer Meadows Metropolitan District, ACC Submittal Form (Application for Modifications or Improvements)
notes: Three-page form read 2026-09-26. The form sends applications to the district's manager by email; that address and phone are left out of copy.

fact: The Masters' covenants define the golf course as Mariana Butte, a public course the City of Loveland owns and runs, and give no owner a right to reach the course or the George Rist Ditch directly from a lot.
quote: “Golf Course” shall mean and refer to Marianna Butte, a public golf course owned and operated by the City of Loveland, Colorado. … no Owner or their guests, licensees or invitees has a right of access to the George Rist Ditch, or the Golf Course directly from their Lot.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, Easements and Restrictions for the Deer Meadows Metropolitan District property (made March 1, 2008), Art. I.K and Sec. 5.3(f)
notes: 'Marianna' is the covenants' spelling.

fact: On Masters lots backing onto Outlot D and the George Rist Ditch, the covenants bar fencing, sheds and permanent landscaping in a 15-foot rear landscape, utility and drainage easement, and let the ditch company remove anything built there at the owner's expense.
quote: SECTION 3.2 A 15 foot private landscape, utility, and drainage easement as depicted on the Plat and located across and upon the rear portions of all Lots backing to Outlot “D” and the George Rist Ditch. No Owner Shall be allowed to construct any permanent structures such as fencing, sheds, or permanent landscaping within this 15 foot easement. Should an Owner construct, or otherwise make improvements within this 15 foot easement, the Consolidated Home Supply Ditch and Reservoir Company shall have the right to remove said improvements at the expense of the Owner
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, Easements and Restrictions for the Deer Meadows Metropolitan District property (made March 1, 2008), Sec. 3.2
notes: The scan's text layer drops the first letter of 'located'; the quote follows the page image.

fact: The Masters' guidelines keep fencing off the rear property line and out of the rear 15-foot landscape easement on Blocks 3, 5 and 7 and on Block 2, Lots 17 and 18, and allow only ranch-rail cedar or black metal fencing elsewhere.
quote: Approved fencing installed by the Owner or builder shall be permitted along the rear lot lines with the following exception: No fencing shall be installed on the rear property line or within the rear 15' landscape easement for Blocks 3,5,7 and Block 2 lots 17-18. … Any fencing approved will only be of the ranch rail cedar or Black Metal variety detailed in Page 10 of this document.
source_label: Deer Meadows Metropolitan District, The Masters at Mariana Butte Architectural and Design Guidelines (Design Criteria updated 6/27/2023), Fencing and Fences

fact: The Masters' guidelines require lots next to the golf course, natural areas and open space to be landscaped to blend into them, bar removing existing trees without the ACC's written approval, and set a 9-month deadline for full landscaping after the certificate of occupancy.
quote: No existing trees shall be removed by any Owner or homebuilder unless approved in writing by the ACC prior to removal. Any existing trees shall be protected during the construction of the home. Complete front, rear and side yard landscape installation shall occur within 9 months of the issuance of a certificate of occupancy. … All lots adjacent to the golf course, natural areas, and open spaces shall incorporate landscaping in such a way as to blend into the adjacent golf course and natural area.
source_label: Deer Meadows Metropolitan District, The Masters at Mariana Butte Architectural and Design Guidelines (Design Criteria updated 6/27/2023), Landscaping
notes: The district's Rules and Regulations (Appendix A, E.2) set six months from closing instead.

fact: The Masters reviews golf-ball protection lot by lot, prefers natural solutions such as trees and bushes or pergola-type structures, and says it will likely reject large poles with netting.
quote: GOLF BALL SAFTEY SYSTEMS: --- Each Owner is responsible for keeping their properties safe from flying objects, District will require any/all structural solutions to be submitted for ACC approval. Each Residence’s location and needs may be different based on placement on golf course, so each case will be reviewed individually and treated as such. It is the intent of the District to be fair allowing for safety while maintaining a consistent aesthetic. In all cases, the District encourages the solutions to be “natural” in character, with trees, bushes and other organic solutions when possible. Pergola type structures may be another feasible alternative. The District will likely reject proposed solutions consisting of large polls with netting.
source_label: Deer Meadows Metropolitan District, The Masters at Mariana Butte Architectural and Design Guidelines (Design Criteria updated 6/27/2023), Golf Ball Safety Systems
notes: 'SAFTEY' and 'polls' are the source's spellings.

fact: The Masters' guidelines bar landscape elements that disturb a lot's finished engineered grading, bar changes to engineered drainage swales, keep drainage directed away from homes, and encourage owners to use soil engineers and landscape professionals.
quote: Site Drainage: No structures or landscape elements shall be placed on the property in a manner that may disturb the finished engineered topography. Finish grading shall not create ponding or washing of water off the site on to adjacent property. The builder, Owner or District shall not modify engineered drainage swales and drainage structures. Drainage shall be directed away from all residential structures. Newly graded areas shall be protected against soil erosion. Owners are encouraged to utilize soil engineers and landscape professionals to help ensure proper drainage is maintained.
source_label: Deer Meadows Metropolitan District, The Masters at Mariana Butte Architectural and Design Guidelines (Design Criteria updated 6/27/2023), Site Drainage

fact: The Masters' guidelines keep landscaping projects on the owner's own lot, bar using district land or neighboring lots for staging, storage, dumping or access, keep delivery trucks off entry and median areas, and limit visible gravel, rock and soil piles to 30 days.
quote: 2. Gravel, rock and/or soil piles left in front or on visible side yards of Lots, in the street, or on the driveway shall be left no longer than a period of thirty days. … 3. Delivery and placement of landscape materials shall not damage District Facilities including entry/median areas. Delivery trucks are not allowed to cross these areas (to avoid sprinkler and landscape damage). … 4. The District Facilities and/or adjacent properties, whether Owner or builder owned, are not to be used in any fashion or manner in any landscaping or project by an Owner. This includes, but is not restricted to, staging, material storage, dumping or access. Landscaping projects are restricted to the property of the Owner undertaking this work.
source_label: Deer Meadows Metropolitan District, The Masters at Mariana Butte Architectural and Design Guidelines (Design Criteria updated 6/27/2023), Landscape and Maintenance

fact: Deer Meadows' rules say work on a lot's improvements may not start before 8 a.m. and must be finished before dusk, set a six-month landscaping deadline after closing, and count landscaping not kept in a healthy, live and growing condition as a violation.
quote: Work shall not be performed prior to 8 a.m. and will need to be completed prior to dusk. 2. Landscape Deadline: Landscaping must be installed by an Owner within six (6) months from the date of original closing with builder. … Failure to maintain landscaping in attractive, healthy, live and growing condition shall be a violation of the governing documents and may be subject to fines and other remedies as provided in the District's governing documents, including Appendix B.
source_label: Deer Meadows Metropolitan District Rules and Regulations (adopted August 2019), Appendix A, E. Maintenance Rules and Regulations
notes: The 8 a.m. to dusk line sits under item 1, Maintenance of Improvements. The cover reads 'ADOPTED 2020' and the footers 'Adopted August 2019'; the six-month deadline differs from the guidelines' nine months after the certificate of occupancy.

fact: Deer Meadows' rules prohibit practicing golf or carrying golf clubs in the district's park.
quote: The District prohibits the following items on or in District Facilities: … b. Practicing golf or having golf clubs in the park.
source_label: Deer Meadows Metropolitan District Rules and Regulations (adopted August 2019), Appendix A, General Regulations for District Facilities, item 21(b)

fact: The Masters allows landscape lighting only with the ACC's written approval, keeps it subdued with the light source hidden from neighboring homes and shielded against spill, and bans uplighting.
quote: Landscape Lighting: No exterior lighting other than that provided by the home builder shall be allowed on any residential lot except with the written approval of the ACC. The ACC may allow subdued exterior landscape lighting, whose light source is not visible from adjoining dwellings, for such purpose as illuminating entrances, decks, driveways, landscaping and parking areas. All lighting shall be shielded to eliminate “spill over” light. No use of up lighting shall be permitted.
source_label: Deer Meadows Metropolitan District, The Masters at Mariana Butte Architectural and Design Guidelines (Design Criteria updated 6/27/2023), Landscape Lighting
notes: A later entry, Lights and Lighting, says builder-style, low-wattage exterior lights need no ACC approval; the two entries read differently for fixtures that match the builder's.

fact: The Masters does not permit dog runs, and sends play and sports equipment to the rear or side yard, generally screened, no taller than 10 feet, with play-yard size judged case by case against the lot and its neighbors.
quote: DOG RUNS — Not Permitted … PLAY AND SPORTS EQUIPMENT - See also Basketball Backboards. ACC approval is required. Equipment shall be located in the rear or side yard generally screened from view. Size of play yards will be considered on a case-by-case basis depending on Lot size and proximity to neighbors. … The maximum height of the equipment should not exceed ten (10) feet. In some cases, written consent from adjacent neighbors may be required.
source_label: Deer Meadows Metropolitan District, The Masters at Mariana Butte Architectural and Design Guidelines (Design Criteria updated 6/27/2023), Dog Runs and Play and Sports Equipment

fact: The Masters requires ACC approval for open patios, for any paving whether walks, driveways or patio areas, and for retaining walls.
quote: PATIOS (OPEN) — ACC approval is required. PAVING — ACC approval is required for installation or changes, regardless of whether for walks, driveways, patio areas or other purposes. … WALLS — RETAINING — ACC approval is required.
source_label: Deer Meadows Metropolitan District, The Masters at Mariana Butte Architectural and Design Guidelines (Design Criteria updated 6/27/2023), Patios, Paving and Walls

fact: Deer Meadows Metropolitan District's service plan describes Mariana Butte Fourteenth Subdivision as the final subdivision in the Mariana Butte P.U.D., about 50 acres and about 77 single-family homes, a golf course community next to Mariana Butte Golf Course.
quote: Deer Meadows is the final subdivision in the Mariana Butte P.U.D. to be developed, and is located entirely within the boundaries of the City of Loveland, Colorado … consisting of approximately fifty (50) acres located entirely within the Loveland city limits … At build-out, the Service Area will contain approximately 77 single family residential units. Deer Meadows is the final subdivision remaining in the Mariana Butte P.U.D. The Development is a golf course community and has several strong amenities, including open space, water features and good views. … adjacent to the Mariana Butte Golf Course.
source_label: Service Plan for Deer Meadows Metropolitan District, City of Loveland (Resolution #R-74-2005)
notes: 38-page scan; its text layer garbles some letters ('co=unity', 'r=aining'), so the quote follows the page image.

fact: Mariana Butte Golf Course, the City of Loveland's 18-hole, 6,583-yard, par-72 course, has holes along the Big Thompson River, a practice putting green at the north end of the lower parking lot and two practice chipping greens with a bunker between the 10th fairway and the 18th green.
quote: Mariana Butte is a premiere, 18-hole course featuring soaring elevated tees, challenging holes that border the rushing Big Thompson River and breathtaking vistas of the Rocky Mountain Front Range. … 18-Hole, 6,583 Yard, Par 72 … Practice Putting Green Mariana Butte has a practice green located at the north end of the lower parking lot. It can be reached directly from the parking lot, or via the cart path from the clubhouse. Practice Chipping Greens Located north of the Clubhouse, at the bottom of the hill between the 10 Fairway and 18 Green, Mariana Butte offers two practice chipping greens with a practice bunker.
source_label: Golf Loveland (City of Loveland), Mariana Butte Golf Course page, read from the Wayback Machine capture of May 9, 2026
notes: The live page returned HTTP 403 to curl on 2026-09-26; read from web.archive.org/web/20260509131602/ of the same URL.

fact: Colorado's business registry lists seven associations named for Mariana Butte in good standing: Mariana Butte Homeowners Association, The Reserve at Mariana Butte Homeowners' Association, The Villages of Mariana Butte Community Association, Mariana Butte Filing No. 11 Homeowners Association, Mariana Butte Filing No. 12 Subassociation, The Ridge at Mariana Butte Association and Mountain Gate at Mariana Butte Association.
quote: MARIANA BUTTE HOMEOWNERS ASSOCIATION, INC. | Good Standing … THE RESERVE AT MARIANA BUTTE HOMEOWNERS' ASSOCIATION, INC. | Good Standing … THE VILLAGES OF MARIANA BUTTE COMMUNITY ASSOCIATION, INC. | Good Standing … MARIANA BUTTE FILING NO. 11 HOMEOWNERS ASSOCIATION, INC. | Good Standing … MARIANA BUTTE FILING NO. 12 SUBASSOCIATION, INC. | Good Standing … THE RIDGE AT MARIANA BUTTE ASSOCIATION | Good Standing … Mountain Gate at Mariana Butte Association | Good Standing
source_label: Colorado Information Marketplace, Business Entities in Colorado (Secretary of State), entity names containing Mariana Butte
notes: Queried the dataset's API (resource 4ykn-tg5h) on 2026-09-26 for names containing MARIANA BUTTE; entity name and status fields quoted. The Mariana Butte Ladies Golf Association (also in good standing) and delinquent or dissolved entities are left out. Deer Meadows Metropolitan District is a special district, not a registered association. Only Deer Meadows and The Reserve were found posting yard rules online.

fact: The Reserve's landscape guidelines start a change with a call to the ARC chair, usually followed by a description and drawings or sketches, and say the ARC may ask for samples or vendor descriptions of products it doesn't know.
quote: Step 1: Contact the ARC Chair that you are considering making a change and confirm what is needed for review and approval. This is usually a description and some drawings or sketches of the change. You might be asked to provide samples or vendor descriptions of products we are not familiar with.
source_label: The Reserve at Mariana Butte HOA Landscape Design Guidelines, updated 2/7/2024, Step 1

fact: The Reserve's guidelines, written to modify the older covenants for xeriscape, let an owner have no natural turf in the front yard though the ARC prefers some drought-resistant turf there, and let three pre-approved xeriscape front-yard designs go in without further review if built unchanged.
quote: Step 2: If you would like to implement some water wise or xeriscape landscape changes, request the latest three pre-approved front yard designs. These don’t require any further review if implemented unchanged. If doing any customization of your design, then ARC review and approval is required. … B. Although some natural turf is preferred in front yards, you are allowed to have no natural turf in your front yard. … This landscape design guidance is intended to maintain a consistent and pleasing neighborhood look, modify previous covenants to incorporate Xeriscape options, and facilitate decreasing water usage. … Having some drought resistant turf in the front yard helps to soften the use of various hardscape materials.
source_label: The Reserve at Mariana Butte HOA Landscape Design Guidelines, updated 2/7/2024, Steps 2 and 3, Introduction and Reserve HOA Preferences

fact: At The Reserve, the city-owned tree lawn along Rossum Drive keeps irrigated grass and Locust trees, and changing it takes HOA approval, unanimous approval from every owner with a tree lawn on Rossum Drive, and City of Loveland Current Planning review.
quote: Note: The City of Loveland wants to maintain a unified look for City owned tree lawn along Rossum Drive. Currently, the City allows only irrigated vegetative turf with the required number of Locust trees. Any change to a tree lawn would require HOA approval and unanimous approval by all homeowners with tree lawns along Rossum Drive and be reviewed and approved by the City of Loveland Current Planning Department.
source_label: The Reserve at Mariana Butte HOA Landscape Design Guidelines, updated 2/7/2024, Pre-approved HOA Approved Front Yard Design Plans

fact: The Reserve's 2002 covenants allow no fences on any lot, require lawn along every lot line so landscaping never marks a boundary, and require lots beside the golf course and natural areas to blend into them so the lot line can't be distinguished.
quote: E. The Declarant further intends to preserve the continuity of landscaping between residential lots and the golf course, natural areas, open spaces, and along streets, and to provide an atmosphere of openness and spaciousness in the subdivision. … (5) Fences are not allowed on any Lot. … (4) Landscaping shall be designed in such a way as to not Delineate any Lot Line. Lawn shall be installed along all Lot Lines and Ground Covering shall not extend to Lot Lines except when designed to extend upon a neighboring Lot with the permission of the neighboring Owner. … (10) Any Lot adjacent to the golf course, General Common Properties, or any Natural Area shall incorporate landscaping in such a way as to blend with the adjacent golf course, General Common Properties, or any Natural Area. The purpose of this provision is to provide that the Lot Lines, which border the golf course, General Common Properties, or any Natural Area shall not be distinguishable.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions for The Reserve at Mariana Butte (made January 17, 2002), Recital E and Art. VI, Sec. 1(a)(5), (e)(4) and (e)(10)

fact: The Reserve's covenants define lawn as sodded or seeded grass, require it within 10 feet of a street lot line, and hold rock, gravel and mulch ground cover to 25% of a lot's landscaping, placed within 15 feet of a structure.
quote: (f) “Ground Cover” shall mean and refer to all rock, gravel, wood chips, mulch or similar ground covering used in landscaping of a Lot. (g) “Lawn” shall mean and refer to the landscaping turf composed of either sodded or seeded grasses, usually consisting of a blend of bluegrass or rye grass. … (3) No Ground Covering shall be placed closer than ten (10) feet to a Lot Line adjacent to a street. Further, no Ground Covering shall make up more than twenty-five percent (25%) of the landscaping on any Lot. All Ground Covering used in the landscaping shall be placed within fifteen (15) feet of the exterior of any structure on a Lot. … (9) Lawn shall be required within ten (10) feet of any Lot Line adjacent to a street.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions for The Reserve at Mariana Butte (made January 17, 2002), Art. I(f) and (g) and Art. VI, Sec. 1(e)(3) and (9)
notes: The 2024 landscape guidelines say they modify previous covenants to incorporate xeriscape, and a 2019 board policy lets Colorado law supersede the covenants where they differ.

fact: The Reserve's covenants allow no protective netting on any lot, expect homes and improvements to be designed for protection from golf balls, want play equipment reasonably screened, allow sheds and gazebos only when attached to the house in its materials, keep statuary and lampposts within 15 feet of the house, and bar unreasonably bright light.
quote: No accessory buildings including sheds, storage structures, outbuildings, greenhouses, gazebos, secondary garages and the like are allowed unless the structure is architecturally compatible, attached to the dwelling, and constructed using the same materials as found in the construction of the dwelling. … (6) Protective netting shall not be allowed on any Lot. Dwellings and other improvements on a Lot shall be designed in such a way as to provide the necessary protection from golf balls or other personal injuries. Clotheslines, unsightly equipment, or equipment intended for children's recreational use such as swing sets and slides shall be placed within the Lot in such a manner as to be reasonably screened from view. … (12) No light shall be emitted from any Lot or dwelling which is unreasonably bright or causes unreasonable glare. … (8) Artistic statuary, sculptures, decorative columns, lampposts, etc. shall be located no more than fifteen (15) feet from a dwelling.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions for The Reserve at Mariana Butte (made January 17, 2002), Art. VI, Sec. 1(a)(3), (a)(6), (a)(12) and (e)(8)

fact: The Reserve's covenants allow no more than three household pets per lot and no dog runs or kennels, and require dog owners to put an underground electric fence around the part of the lot where a dog moves freely.
quote: (c) Pets. No more than three (3) generally recognized domestic house or yard pets shall be allowed on any Lot. … All Owners with a dog shall have an underground electric fence around that area of their Lot in which they allow their dog freedom to move without a chain, leash, or other restraint. Kennels shall not be allowed on the Property and no dog runs shall be allowed on any Lot.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions for The Reserve at Mariana Butte (made January 17, 2002), Art. VI, Sec. 1(c)

fact: The Reserve's covenants set up a three-member ARC, start a 30-day review clock when it confirms in writing that a submission is complete, presume plans approved if it doesn't act by then, and say its approval is not building-code compliance.
quote: (a) There is hereby established an Architectural Review Committee consisting of three (3) members. … (d) If the Architectural Review Committee fails either to approve or to disapprove such plans and specifications (including resubmission of disapproved plans and specifications which have been revised) within thirty (30) days after the same have been submitted to it (provided that all required information has been submitted), it shall be conclusively presumed that said plans and specifications have been approved subject, however, to the restrictions contained in Article VI hereof. The Architectural Review Committee shall notify the Owner in Writing upon receipt of all required plans and specifications and the aforesaid thirty (30) day period shall commence on the date of such notification. … Approval by the Architectural Review Committee shall not be deemed to constitute compliance with the requirements of any required building codes
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions for The Reserve at Mariana Butte (made January 17, 2002), Art. V, Sec. 1(a), (d) and (e)

fact: A January 2019 Reserve board policy has the ARC weigh both the covenants and Colorado law in landscape decisions, with Colorado law superseding the covenants where they differ.
quote: ARC, in reviewing and approving any landscape plans or issues, shall use both the HOA covenants and all pertinent Colorado law in making determinations. Colorado law will supersede the HOA covenants in case of differences. This shall include landscaping and its uses on member lots.
source_label: The Reserve at Mariana Butte HOA, Board of Directors Policy # 2019-1, Xeriscaping (approved January 25, 2019)
notes: One-page scan with no text layer; read from the page image on 2026-09-26. The policy says it does not apply to HOA common areas.

fact: The Reserve's owner information describes an open design theme that blends with the river-area landscape, with no structures or landscaping marking property lines so wildlife can roam.
quote: Design: The general design theme of The Reserve is to be open, blending with natural conditions along this river area in Colorado. This is the reason there are no structures or landscaping demarcating property lines. This also provides for the free roaming of wildlife, which is plentiful.
source_label: The Reserve at Mariana Butte HOA, 2025 welcome letter and Owner Information (February 2024)
notes: The letter also names board and ARC members with their phone numbers and emails; none of that goes into copy.

fact: The Reserve's owner information says anything visible, landscaping included, needs the ARC's approval before a significant change, that sprinkler changes, trimming and replanting flowers generally aren't significant while removing or replanting a tree is, and that the board and ARC walk the neighborhood each year, usually in late spring.
quote: The outside appearance of properties is managed by the Architectural Review Committee (ARC). This includes anything visible, from roofs to building elevations to landscaping. Owners must contact the ARC to obtain approval before making any significant changes. Significant changes would be something visible. Sprinkler modifications, trimming, or replanting flowers aren't generally significant. Removal or replanting a tree would be significant. … Annual Walk Through: The board and ARC conduct an annual walk-about inspection, usually in late spring.
source_label: The Reserve at Mariana Butte HOA, 2025 welcome letter and Owner Information (February 2024)

fact: The Reserve's owner information says some homes next to Mariana Butte Golf Course get flying golf balls, that damage is the responsibility of whoever hit the ball, that golf treats a home lot as out of bounds, and that several homes sit next to or within a flood plain.
quote: You are living in a golf community. Some homes adjacent to the Mariana Butte Golf course experience flying golf balls. Damage is the responsibility of the person who hits the golf ball. … Per the rules of golf, the homeowner property is treated as out of bounds so no golfer should be hitting from there. … Several of our homes are located adjacent to or within a flood plain and it is up to each homeowner to understand their location.
source_label: The Reserve at Mariana Butte HOA, 2025 welcome letter and Owner Information (February 2024)

fact: The Reserve's 91 lots sit in three subdivisions beside the city-owned Morey Nature Reserve (20 acres) and the roughly 78-acre Ward property, with Dry Creek running through the neighborhood and the HOA maintaining about 300 feet of the George Rist Irrigation Ditch, which can carry water from April to November.
quote: We have 91 member lots in 3 subdivisions (1st, 2nd, and 4th). All are single family homes. The Reserve is one of several HOAs in the area surrounding the golf course. The Morey Nature Reserve (20 acres), and the “Ward property” (approximately 78 acres of nature conservancy) at the end of Cedar Valley Drive are owned by City of Loveland. Dry Creek flows through our HOA. … George Rist Irrigation Ditch: On the west side of our HOA is the George Rist Irrigation Ditch. The HOA is responsible for about 300’ of the concrete-lined ditch and bank areas. … There can be water flowing in the ditch from April to November
source_label: The Reserve at Mariana Butte HOA, 2025 welcome letter and Owner Information (February 2024)
